recipes.name: Quick and Easy Black Bean Soup
ingredients_raw: 2 (14.5 ounce) cans black beans, rinsed and drained
2 teaspoons sambal paste (or minced red chiles)

steps.text: Place bacon in a cold pot. Turn heat to medium, cook and stir until the bacon is cooked but not crisp.
Stir in onion; cook and stir for 5 minutes, until the onion turns translucent and golden.
Stir in garlic; cook for 2-3 minutes. Add chicken stock, turn heat to medium-high. Stir in oregano, cayenne and salt. Add black beans and water. Return to a simmer.
Simmer on medium-low, stirring occasionally, for 20-30 minutes. While it's cooking, mash about half the beans to thicken the soup.
Stir in black pepper and cumin. Add salt to taste.
Make the relish by stirring together minced green onion, sambal paste, and lime juice.
Serve garnished with relish, chopped green onions, and sour cream.

raw_recipe.headline: Quick and Easy Black Bean Soup
raw_recipe.description: All you need is a couple cans of beans, an onion, some bacon, and spices to whip up this simple but delicious soup.

review.reviewBody: This was quite good. I left out the bacon to cut calories and replaced the can of water with more chicken broth to up the flavor. Came out delicious. Do make the garnish and use either sour cream or yogurt to top it off. Black beans are so healthy so any way to incorporate them into your diet is a winner - if it's tasty too than all the better!
WOW. This soup is bursting with flavor and is rather easy to throw together. I added some celery, shallots instead of onion , used peppered- uncured bacon and pureed about half the soup. So good.

I made this soup and it was delicious. I added in a few diced carrots and used Chicken Stock instead of water. I used fresh Sage and Oregano from my garden --approx 3 T Oregano and 1 T Sage -- a pinch of cumin, salt and pepper to taste. I cooked it overnight in Slow Cooker and in the morning I mashed the beans and carrots with a potato masher and served the soup at noon to a friend I'd invited for lunch. I served Corn Bread and fresh-made Raspberry jam with the soup. I'd make it again. My friend liked the soup a lot.

I made this, and just came back to make sure I had saved it. This is a very good black bean soup. The only thing I did differently was to use the immersion blender. I took out half the beans, used the blender, then returned the full beans to the pot. The flavors are are spot on! We had cheese quesadillas with it. Yummy

I love Chef John recipes but as a seasoned cook (pun intended) no matter how hard I try I always manage to put my own spin on it so often ends up being a solid guideline. In any event, for this recipe I followed it but doubled it and used an entire pound of WELL TRIMMED bacon, degreased the pan sans a tablespoon or so of drippings then added carrots and celery sauteed with the onion. Beside the oregano (great addition CJ - TY!) a tablespoon worchestershire and lime juice. Used homemade chicken broth throughout (i,e., no water), added a can of refried black beans and then 3 cans rinsed whole black beans. This worked well rather than mashing them in the pot. Topped it with a mix of sliced green onion and jalapenos, shredded cheddar and a dollop of sour cream. Thankfully to rave reviews. Thank you Chef John !!

This recipe is delicious!!
I added a bell pepper, a red pepper, and 2 onions rather than 1, and it added a great amount of flavor!! I also added a 3rd can of black beans.
Instead of making a relish, I mixed the lime juice and the Sambal Paste together and added that into the soup when I put in the water. 
Also, I diced and crisped up some bacon on the side to add on top of the soup, along with sour cream and avocado on the side to add in as well. 
Everyone came back for more and it was gone by the end of the evening! lol. This is my new favorite recipe to cook, and to eat - for sure!! 
Thank you for this delicious recipe!!!!! A++++++

I really do love this recipe. I've made it as is and it was great. However, recently when I make this I use this recipe as a foundation but add to it. I used 4 cans of black beans (so I doubled everything) I throw a whole onion, several cloves of garlic, one green bellpepper, one red bell pepper, several serrano peppers, and 12 strips of bacon into a pan to cook. After that's done I throw it all into a crock pot to slow cook together for a few hours. It really is an amazing spicy and smoky black bean soup. I also mash up the beans a good bit while they're in the crock pot. I don't like the soup completely pureed, but I do like it to be thicker than a brothy soup.

This soup is delicious, I've made it several times. My sister begs for it every time I have her over. The only changes since following the recipe exactly the first time is, I cook the bacon, set aside, cook the onion & garlic in the bacon fat, drain the fat, and use my blender versus potato masher . I have to double the relish because it's sooo popular, and for the garnish, I cut up avocado, have sour cream, and chop up that cooked bacon. Thanks Chef John!

So I already had a pound of dry black beans soaking when I found this recipe, so I adapted the recipe for that, and I used chicken bone broth. I had two cans of black beans on hand, so I pureed those and added them to the pot but still ended up pureeing a lot of the beans and reducing the soup to get the consistency that I wanted. I used plain goat yogurt instead of sour cream, and that worked nicely. I also added some cilantro at the end. Yummy!

Loved it! I cut the bacon (just used 2 slices) and just did avocado for the relish/ garnish. I substitutes extra chicken stock instead of water and added an extra can of beans. So yummy. Served over a little bed of white rice w cheddar cheese and sour cream. Yum!!

I’ve made this a few times now, and doubled the recipe this time because I love it so much and like to freeze it in portions for lunches. The only change I made with the seasoning is to use Herb de Province instead of Orgeano. I did not double the bacon, however-I used six slices of quality bacon from the butcher. I also scooped out most beans and puréed in my manual food processor. This recipe is a keeper!
So simple and sooooo good! Added some fresh corn for color and a bit of flavor!
Too much liquid no need to add the water otherwise good did add fresh corn and a tomato

It’s easy and tastes great. Very comforting. High protein. I didn’t have cumin so I replaced it with smoked paprika. I also used an emersion blender, because my masher wasn’t good enough. I left the room and returned to see the whole pot emptied. Will definitely add to our regular rotation.
The taste hits the spot. Next time I will blenderize half the beans beforehand. Otherwise, it's mouthfuls of skins and no full beans to enjoy.
I would modify next time and use a fee ounces less water.
I made this it's absolutely delicious!
Really easy and delicious. followed recipe to the letter and my whole family complimented the"chef"

An absolute winner and super easy to make! I happened to have all the ingredients on hand, so went ahead and made it. My only changes were using canned Cuban Black Beans (pre-seasoned) and throwing in some leftover corn, bacon and some mashed potatoes to thicken it up. Mashing the beans made all the difference!
